title: Cracked TiO2 Photoanode Coating
introduction: Cracked TiO2 photoanode coating is the structural failure of the TiO2 layer in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) when crack networks form through the deposited film. In layers fabricated by electrophoretic deposition (EPD), bubble-induced pores act as stress concentration sites during drying and sintering, driving crack propagation that produces a fractured, discontinuous photoanode. The cracks disrupt the transport pathways for photo-generated electrons through the TiO2 network to the external circuit, directly reducing short-circuit current and overall conversion efficiency. Crack width and film separation from the substrate are observed to be greater in EPD films than in doctor-blade control films.
reasoning: The 697-Elsevier DSSC study directly reports cracked TiO2 layers as the observable failure outcome of EPD bubble-induced pore stress concentration, with reduced Isc and conversion efficiency as the measured performance consequences.

key_findings.claim: Cracks appearing in EPD-fabricated TiO2 layers reduce short-circuit current and overall conversion efficiency
key_findings.detail: A decrease in short-circuit current (Isc) and efficiency is directly attributed to the TiO2 layer thickness and the cracks appearing in the layer fabricated with the EPD technique. [^elsevier697a] These cracks would result in decreasing of overall conversion efficiency of the DSSC. [^elsevier697b]
